newsitem.title: POLAND: Greek president supports Poland's NATO, EU goals.
newsitem.headline: Greek president supports Poland's NATO, EU goals.

text.p: Costis Stephanopoulos, beginning the first visit by a Greek president to Poland, on Monday restated his country's support for Warsaw's key foreign policy goals of joining NATO and the European Union.

"We agreed on the future of Europe -- that there is a need for the countries of eastern and central Europe to join the European Union," Stephanopoulos told reporters after talks in Warsaw with his counterpart Aleksander Kwasniewski.
"We agreed NATO plays a stabilising role in Europe and that countries which wish to should be able to enter it," he added.
Stephanopoulos is accompanied on the three-day official visit by Greek business executives and he said he hoped the trip would boost trade and Greek investment in Poland.

The Polish president was asked to comment on Cyprus, with which Greece has a joint defence pact. Turkey invaded the northern third of Cyprus in 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup, and tensions there have risen markedly there this year.
Kwasniewski told reporters that Poland supported all moves which involved dialogue and was against all aggression.
"Everything which serves to resolve the Cyprus problem, to build good relations between Turkey and Greece, wins our support," Kwasniewski said.
Kwasniewski said Poland hoped to start talks on its own EU entry early in 1998, while recognising that Cyprus and Malta were front-runners to join.

"We believe that Cyprus and Malta will begin these (EU) negotiations and that on January 1, 1998 the first group of eastern and central European countries, including Poland, will also begin the talks," he said.
Stephanopoulos is due to hold talks with Poland's prime minister and foreign minister on Tuesday, and to address parliament's foreign affairs committees.
On Wednesday he is to lay flowers at the World War Two Nazi German death camps of Auschwitz and Birkenau in southern Poland.
